name: Tainted Memorandum
summary: A quiet message draws a young gnome warlock toward the shadows of Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm passes it along, and Alamar Grimm calls the neophyte to learn dark power and rely on it rather than their dwarven hosts.

sections.title: A Discreet Summons
sections.body: In Coldridge Valley, the dark arts meet deep suspicion. While you help Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, he slips you a note. His reluctance shows the uneasy truce that lets warlocks practice in Alliance lands. He warns you to watch yourself because your kind is not trusted around these parts.

sections.title: Gnomish Bitterness in Exile
sections.body: Inside Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm speaks plainly about the gnomes' plight. He believes conventional tinkering and ordinary magic failed Gnomeregan, bringing their people near extinction and leaving them as second-class refugees dependent on dwarven goodwill. He urges you to rely neither on the Holy Light nor on dwarven politics. Instead, he teaches you to summon and master fiends, whose obedience is unconditional.

faq.answer: It is a written message Sten Stoutarm hands to novice gnome warlocks in Coldridge Valley. It directs them to seek Alamar Grimm, the warlock trainer in Anvilmar.

faq.q: Why are warlocks distrusted in Coldridge Valley?
faq.answer: Dwarves and their Alliance allies prize martial honor and the Holy Light. They regard demonology and shadow magic as corrupt and dangerous, leaving gnome warlocks under deep suspicion.
Alamar Grimm is a gnome warlock trainer in Anvilmar. Bitter over Gnomeregan's fall and reliance on dwarven charity, he teaches young gnomes to bind demonic minions and claim power for themselves.

faq.q: Why does Grimm criticize normal magic and technology?
faq.answer: Grimm believes conventional engineering and accepted schools of magic failed the gnomes in the disaster at Gnomeregan. He says this left them dependent on dwarf patrons who put ties with humans ahead of reclaiming the gnome homeland.

faq.q: Can dwarf warlocks receive this quest?
faq.answer: No. In Dun Morogh, only gnomes can practice the warlock path, so this summons is for newly arrived gnome practitioners.

faq.q: Where does this quest take place?
faq.answer: You begin near Sten Stoutarm in Coldridge Valley and finish inside Anvilmar, the central redoubt overlooking the valley in southwestern Dun Morogh.

angles.text: As a warlock, you receive a missive marking your formal entry into the craft. It frames demonic pacts as a practical choice born of survival, not madness.
As a gnome, you may share the resentment some exiles feel over losing their home and depending on Ironforge.
As a dwarf, you see your people tolerate these dark practitioners under their roof with obvious distaste and sharp wariness.
